body:
Found 2026-08-09 during the annotation write-back investigation. Full context: workspace
`notes/KOBO-ANNOTATIONS-WRITEBACK-INVESTIGATION-2026-08-09.md`.

`ub.Annotation.content_id` is populated with two mutually unintelligible string formats depending
only on how the annotation reached us:

- **Device PATCH path** synthesizes `f"{uuid}!!{chapter_filename}"`
  (`cps/services/annotation_sync/__init__.py:177-180`) — e.g. `b3d1b38b-...!!chapter6.html`.
- **Uploaded `KoboReader.sqlite` path** stores the device's raw `ContentID` verbatim
  (`cps/annotations.py:216`, from `cps/services/kobo_import.py`) — e.g.
  `file:///mnt/onboard/Author/Title.epub#(6)OEBPS/cha01.xhtml`.

Same book, same chapter, same user, two unrelated strings. Nothing normalizes between them.

Impact: any keying, grouping, dedupe, or chapter-level query on `content_id` is silently wrong
across the two populations. A user who both syncs a Kobo AND imports their `KoboReader.sqlite`
(which we actively invite — it's the documented recovery path, and we recommended it publicly on
janeczku/calibre-web#2610) gets two disjoint sets of annotations for the same chapters with no
indication they're related. It will present as "my highlights are duplicated / don't match" long
after anyone remembers why.

Also relevant to the SPA web-reader rebuild now in progress, which consumes this column.

NOT established: whether any current code path actually joins on `content_id` in a way that
produces a user-visible bug today — the grouping in the annotations view orders by
`chapter_progress`, not `content_id`. So this may currently be latent. It is still a real
correctness hazard for anything built on the column, which is why it is filed rather than fixed.

Fix direction (not applied — the investigation was research-only and gated against schema/sync-path
changes): normalize at ingest to one canonical shape, and decide whether the raw device form needs
preserving separately for round-trip. Note `device_origin_id` already exists for device-side
identity, which may be the right home for the raw form.
title: content_id holds two incompatible shapes depending on ingest path
